gaps.sentence: Even after she moved abroad, we ___ in touch by email.
gaps.explanation: keep in touch means to maintain contact with someone.

gaps.sentence: We ___ a taxi from the airport because it was raining.
gaps.explanation: take a taxi/bus/train is the standard collocation for using transport.

gaps.sentence: She ___ a quick shower before leaving the gym.
gaps.explanation: have a shower is the standard British English collocation; 'made a shower' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: I was nearly late, but I managed to ___ the last bus.
gaps.hint: to get on a bus or train in time
gaps.explanation: catch a bus/train means to arrive in time to board it; the words 'managed to' and 'nearly late' show success.

gaps.sentence: Shall we split it, or will you ___ the bill?
gaps.explanation: pay the bill is the fixed collocation in restaurants; 'spend the bill' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: It ___ no difference whether we leave today or tomorrow.
gaps.explanation: 'Make no difference' is the fixed phrase.

gaps.sentence: There was ___ fog at the airport all morning.
gaps.explanation: thick fog (or dense fog) is the standard collocation; 'strong fog' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: Her company ___ a huge profit last year.
gaps.explanation: make a profit (or make a loss) is the fixed business collocation.
